chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn al-Qalanisi, or some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The servant may make an exception in his oath for a period between himself and forty days if he forgets."

key_terms.يَسْتَثْنِيَ: To make an exception / stipulate a condition

ai.seo_question: What is the maximum grace period allowed for fulfilling an oath if one forgets the deadline?
ai.summary: Reported by Shaykh al-Tusi in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the juristic principle that forgetfulness grants the oath-taker a grace period of up to forty days to fulfill their vow, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ease (*yusr*) in legal obligations. It underscores the distinction between intentional breach and unintentional delay, a key nuance in *fiqh al-yaman* (jurisprudence of oaths).
